facts.statement: The only known specimen of Arminisaurus is a fragmentary skeleton that is about 40 percent complete, including an incomplete lower jaw, teeth, vertebrae, and parts of the pectoral girdle and paddles.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen is a fragmentary skeleton (about 40 percent complete), comprising an incomplete lower jaw, teeth, vertebrae and elements from the pectoral girdle and the paddles.

facts.statement: Arminisaurus had an estimated body length of 3 to 4 meters.
facts.quote: The animal had an estimated body length of 3-4 m.

facts.statement: The holotype of Arminisaurus was discovered in the early 1980s by fossil collector Lothar Schulz in the abandoned clay pit Beukenhorst II in the Bielefeld district of Jöllenbeck.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in the early 1980s by the Hannover-based fossil collector Lothar Schulz in the now abandoned clay pit Beukenhorst II, located in the Bielefeld district of Jöllenbeck.

facts.statement: Arminisaurus schuberti was formally described in 2018 by paleontologists Sven Sachs and Benjamin Kear.
facts.quote: Arminisaurus schuberti was described in 2018 by Sven Sachs and Benjamin Kear.

facts.statement: The genus name Arminisaurus honors Arminius, the Cherusci chieftain who defeated three Roman legions in 9 AD, as a tribute to the region where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: The generic name Arminisaurus refers to Arminius, chieftain of the Cherusci tribe who defeated three Roman legions in the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest in 9 AD and is a homage to the region where the specimen was found.

facts.statement: The species name schuberti honors amateur paleontologist Siegfried Schubert for his contributions to the geology of the Bielefeld region.
facts.quote: The species name schuberti honours Siegfried Schubert for his contributions (including numerous scientific publications), enhancing the knowledge of the geology of the Bielefeld region.

facts.statement: Arminisaurus is classified as a member of the family Pliosauridae, a group of plesiosaurs known from the Early Jurassic to the early Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis found Arminisaurus schuberti to be a member of the family Pliosauridae, a globally distributed plesiosaurian clade that is known from the Early Jurassic to the early Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Arminisaurus is considered a basal pliosaurid, distinguished from other members of its clade by specific characteristics in the mandible, neck vertebrae, and scapula.
facts.quote: Arminisaurus was a basal pliosaurid and differs from other members of the clade by a combination of characters found in the mandible, the neck vertebrae and the scapula.

facts.statement: Arminisaurus lived during the Pliensbachian stage, approximately 192.9 to 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pliensbachian to Pliensbachian (192.9 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Arminisaurus is one of only three plesiosaurian taxa described from the Pliensbachian stage, alongside Westphaliasaurus and Cryonectes.
facts.quote: With Westphaliasaurus and Cryonectes, Arminisaurus is only the third plesiosaurian taxon that was described from the Pliensbachian stage.

rejected.statement: Arminisaurus is a genus of pliosaurid plesiosaur that lived during the Lower Jurassic in what is now Germany.
rejected.quote: Arminisaurus (meaning "lizard of Arminius") is a genus of pliosaurid plesiosaur that lived during the Lower Jurassic in present-day Germany.
